body.statement:
For the former widening longitudinal density
\[
w_T(x)=\frac{15}{16T}\left(1-\frac{x^2}{T^2}\right)^2\mathbf 1\{|x|\le T\},
\]
assume \(\alpha_n(3T+2\varepsilon)\le1\).  Then
\[
\max_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}G_n(r)
\ge \frac{25T}{128}+\frac{15\varepsilon}{256}.
\]
In particular, for the former schedules \(T_n=2^{\lfloor(\log_2n)/12\rfloor}\) and \(\varepsilon_n=T_n^{-1}\), the left-hand side tends to infinity.  Consequently no finite \(\mathfrak L^\dagger\) and no sequence \(e_n\to0\) can satisfy \(\max_rG_n(r)\le\mathfrak L^\dagger+e_n\) along those schedules.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(\vartheta(t)=(c^\dagger)^\top t\).  The positivity premise and \(\mathrm{prop:unequal\text{-}three\text{-}arm\text{-}exact\text{-}primitives}\) make every \(p_{n,x,h}^\dagger\) a probability distribution, hence make the displayed mixture a genuine prior.  Conditional on \((X^\dagger,H^\dagger)=(x,h)\), the labeled response types are independent with common law \(p_{n,x,h}^\dagger\).  Indeed, for a labeled type sequence with count vector \(m\), multiplication of its multinomial-count probability by the reciprocal orbit size gives
\[
\left\{\frac{n!}{\prod_tm_t!}\prod_t
 (p_{n,x,h,t}^\dagger)^{m_t}\right\}
\left\{\frac{\prod_tm_t!}{n!}\right\}
=\prod_{i=1}^np_{n,x,h,t_i}^\dagger. \tag{1}
\]
This calculation also keeps the target equal to the realized finite-population contrast
\(n^{-1}\sum_i\vartheta(t_i)\); it does not replace that target by a prior mean.

The exact-primitives proposition gives the positive-measure equalities
\[
\sum_t\lambda_{v,t}^+\vartheta(t)^2=\frac58,
\qquad
\sum_t\lambda_{d,t}^+\vartheta(t)^2=\frac3{16}.
\]
Complementing a type changes \(\vartheta(t)\) to \(-\vartheta(t)\), by the zero-sum contrast assumption, and the displayed negative measures are the complements of the positive ones.  Hence
\[
\sum_t\lambda_{v,t}^-\vartheta(t)^2=\frac58,
\qquad
\sum_t\lambda_{d,t}^-\vartheta(t)^2=\frac3{16}. \tag{2}
\]
The central types \(000\) and \(111\) have zero score.  Substitution in the definition of \(p_{n,x,h}^\dagger\) therefore yields the exact conditional second moment
\[
\mathbb E\{\vartheta(t_i)^2\mid x,h\}
=\alpha_n\left(\frac58|x|+\frac3{16}|h|\right). \tag{3}
\]
Direct integration of the two polynomial densities gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E|X^\dagger|
&=\frac{30}{16T}\int_0^Tx\left(1-\frac{x^2}{T^2}\right)^2dx
=\frac{5T}{16},\\
\mathbb E|H^\dagger|
&=\frac{30}{16\varepsilon}\int_0^\varepsilon h
 \left(1-\frac{h^2}{\varepsilon^2}\right)^2dh
=\frac{5\varepsilon}{16}. \tag{4}
\end{aligned}
\]

Now assign units independently with probabilities
\(q^\dagger=(1/2,1/8,3/8)\).  Every component is positive.  Define
\[
Z_i=\frac{c_{A_i}^\dagger\{Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}-1/2\}}
 {q_{A_i}^\dagger},
\qquad
\overline\tau_{\mathrm{HT}}=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^nZ_i.
\]
For every fixed schedule, the zero-sum and \(\ell^1\)-normalization assumptions imply
\[
\mathbb E_AZ_i=\vartheta(t_i),
\qquad
\mathbb E_AZ_i^2
=\sum_{a=1}^3\frac{(c_a^\dagger)^2}{4q_a^\dagger}
=\frac12\sum_{a=1}^3|c_a^\dagger|=1. \tag{5}
\]
Independence across units now gives
\[
\mathbb E_A\!\left[
 \{\overline\tau_{\mathrm{HT}}-\tau_{c^\dagger}(y)\}^2
 \mid y\right]
=\frac1{n^2}\sum_{i=1}^n\{1-\vartheta(t_i)^2\}. \tag{6}
\]
Average (6) under the genuine prior and use (3)--(4) and
\(\alpha_n=n^{-1/3}\).  The result is
\[
\operatorname{BayesRisk}(\overline\tau_{\mathrm{HT}})
=\frac1n-n^{-4/3}\left(\frac{25T}{128}
 +\frac{15\varepsilon}{256}\right). \tag{7}
\]
The normalization assumptions put every target in \([-1,1]\), so projection of
\(\overline\tau_{\mathrm{HT}}\) onto \([-1,1]\) cannot increase squared error.
Conditional on its allocation count \(r\), the independent design is uniform over labeled assignments having that count.  Posterior square completion in
\(\mathrm{def:exact\text{-}tube\text{-}bayes\text{-}risk}\) says that
\(\mathcal B_{n,\varepsilon,T}^\dagger(r)\) is the minimum conditional Bayes risk.  If \(\pi\) is the induced count law, then
\[
B_{n,\varepsilon,T}^\dagger
\le\sum_r\pi(r)\mathcal B_{n,\varepsilon,T}^\dagger(r)
\le\frac1n-n^{-4/3}\left(\frac{25T}{128}
 +\frac{15\varepsilon}{256}\right). \tag{8}
\]
The first inequality says that a minimum is no larger than a convex average; the second compares the posterior mean with the clipped estimator above.  By the definitions of \(B_{n,\varepsilon,T}^\dagger\) and \(G_n\), (8) is equivalent to
\[
\max_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}G_n(r)
=n^{4/3}\left\{\frac1n-B_{n,\varepsilon,T}^\dagger\right\}
\ge\frac{25T}{128}+\frac{15\varepsilon}{256}. \tag{9}
\]

For the former schedules, \(T_n\le n^{1/12}\), \(T_n\to\infty\), and
\(\varepsilon_n=T_n^{-1}\).  Hence
\[
\alpha_n(3T_n+2\varepsilon_n)
\le3n^{-1/4}+2n^{-1/3}\longrightarrow0, \tag{10}
\]
so the positivity premise holds eventually.  Applying (9) gives
\[
\max_rG_n(r)\ge\frac{25T_n}{128}+\frac{15}{256T_n}
\longrightarrow\infty. \tag{11}
\]
If a finite \(\mathfrak L^\dagger\) and \(e_n\to0\) obeyed the asserted uniform upper bound, its right-hand side would remain bounded, contradicting (11).  This proves every clause.
body.justification: This exact witness prevents the invalid widening prior from being reused in any sharp-limit proof.
body.gap: It refutes one prior family and does not decide the corrected compact Airy-tube bridge.
body.consumer: The corrected root theorem and honest-scope narrative use it to separate the failed construction from the surviving design question.
